title: Urgent bug in the middle of a feature

scenario.brief:
You are halfway through a date-range filter for the sales report on `feature/report-filters`. `src/filters.js` has an unfinished `byDateRange` function with a TODO in it. It does not work yet and the team rule is clear: no half-finished code gets committed to a shared branch, because CI runs on every push.

A customer-facing bug just came in with priority. `formatMonth` in `src/dates.js` prints the wrong month in every report header because `getUTCMonth()` is zero-based and nobody added one. The fix belongs on `main` today.

Park your unfinished filter work safely, fix the bug on `main` with a focused commit (a short-lived `hotfix/...` branch merged into `main` is fine too), then return to `feature/report-filters` and restore your work exactly as it was, still uncommitted. Leave no stash entries behind.
scenario.whyItMatters: Context switches are constant in real teams. The stash lets you set work aside in seconds without committing something broken or losing it. Knowing when to stash versus when to commit a work-in-progress is a judgement every engineer makes weekly.

steps.author: priya
steps.message: Add sales report with month header

files.README.md:
# Ledgerly

Invoices and sales reports for Ledgerly customers.

objectives.title: Fix formatMonth on main without including the unfinished filter work
hints: You cannot switch to main while src/filters.js has changes that would be overwritten, and you must not commit them. Set them aside first.
`git stash` saves your tracked changes and cleans the working tree. Then `git switch main`, edit src/dates.js so the month is `d.getUTCMonth() + 1`, and commit.
Run `git stash`, `git switch main`, fix the line, then `git commit -am "Fix off-by-one month in report header"`

objectives.title: Return to feature/report-filters with byDateRange restored and still uncommitted
hints: Switch back to your feature branch, then bring the parked changes back into the working tree.
`git stash pop` applies the most recent stash and removes it from the list. `git stash list` shows what is parked.
Run `git switch feature/report-filters` then `git stash pop`. `git diff` should show byDateRange again.

objectives.title: Leave no stash entries behind
hints: `apply` keeps the stash entry; `pop` removes it after applying.
If you used `git stash apply`, remove the entry with `git stash drop` once you are sure the changes are back.
Check with `git stash list`; it should print nothing.

debrief.summary: You parked unfinished work, shipped a focused fix on main, and restored your work exactly as it was, with nothing half-done committed to a shared branch.
internals: `git stash` created two hidden commits: one capturing the index and one capturing the working tree, parented on your branch tip, and pointed `refs/stash` at them. It then reset your working tree to HEAD.
Switching to main was now safe because no tracked file had local modifications.
Your fix commit on main has only src/dates.js in its diff; the filter work never touched main's history.
`git stash pop` merged the stashed tree back onto your current HEAD and dropped the stash ref. Because the branch had not moved, it applied cleanly as unstaged changes.

keyCommands.note: Park tracked changes. Add `-u` to include untracked files, `-m` to label it.
Restore the latest entry and drop it. `apply` restores but keeps it.
Inspect what a stash contains before applying it.

commonMistakes: Committing the half-finished work "temporarily" on the shared branch; CI goes red for everyone.
Forgetting that untracked files are not stashed by default, then switching branches with them in the way.
Running `git stash` on one branch and `git stash pop` on another without meaning to. It usually applies, but can conflict.
Accumulating a dozen anonymous stashes. Label them (`-m`) or turn long-lived ones into a branch (`git stash branch`).
debrief.atWork: Interrupt-driven work is normal: incidents, review requests, a teammate who needs a quick fix. Being able to context-switch in under a minute, without losing anything, is what makes you dependable under pressure.
debrief.interview: "You are mid-feature and production is broken. What do you do?" Describe stashing (or a WIP commit on your own branch), fixing on the right branch, and restoring your context, including why you would not commit broken code to a shared branch.

solution: git commit -am "Fix off-by-one month in report header"
